[[:File:T1 Worlds25 Skins Splash Art.jpg|T1 Galio]] |history={{THA}} }} {{PlayerIntro}} He is the most decorated player of all time. Faker has won six [[World Championship]]s ([[World Championship/2013|2013]], [[World Championship/2015|2015]], [[World Championship/2016|2016]], [[World Championship/2023|2023]], [[World Championship/2024|2024]], [[World Championship/2025|2025]], the most of any player) and two [[Mid-Season Invitational]]s ([[Mid-Season Invitational/2016|2016]], [[Mid-Season Invitational/2017|2017]]), and has 10 combined [[LCK]] and [[LoL_Champions_Korea|Champions Korea]] titles. He is sometimes referred to as "The Unkillable Demon King" by Korean fans.{{cite web | url = https://www.theplayerstribune.com/articles/faker-league-of-legends-worlds-unkillable | title = Unkillable | author = [[Faker]] | date = 2016-10-28 | publisher = [https://www.theplayerstribune.com The Players' Tribune] | accessdate = 2021-10-03 }} On May 22nd, 2024, Faker was announced as the inaugural inductee into the [[Hall of Legends]] by LoL Esports. He was officially inducted at The Shilla Seoul in South Korea on June 6th, 2024. {{cite web|url=https://lolesports.com/article/lol-esports-welcomes-faker-to-hall-of-legends/blt71dc04544f535ae0|title=LoL Esports Welcomes Faker to Hall of Legends|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2024-05-22|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}}{{cite web|url=https://x.com/T1LoL/status/1798995814972617041|title=Congratulations to ‘Faker’ for being inducted into the Hall of Legends|author=[[T1]]|date=2024-06-07}} {{Quote |quote = "For more than 12 years, Faker has shown incredible dedication to the game and sport. As the mid-laner for T1, Faker has long been known for his technical prowess and his ability to make game-changing plays earning him the moniker “The Unkillable Demon King.” His individual skill and in-game leadership have led his teams to numerous victories, having earned 10 LCK titles, two Mid-Season Invitational titles, and four World Championship titles.

“Faker is truly the most iconic and influential figure in League of Legends and esports history,” said John Needham, President of Esports at Riot Games. “His name is synonymous with excellence in LoL Esports, and he has rightfully earned his place as our very first Hall of Legends inductee.”"|sign =-LoL Esports |source = }} {{SectionLinks |achievementsHeader=Achievements |awardsHeader=Awards |biographyHeader=Biography |mediaHeader=Media |triviaHeader=Trivia }} ==Achievements== {{Player achievements table}} ==Statistics== {{Player statistics table}} ==Awards== {{player awards table}} ==Biography== {{Want_to_Help |issue=Add sections on other years of Faker's career |fix=add a short history of 1-2 paragraphs to each year with references and hyperlinks (look at established player pages for inspiration) |date=2024-07-10 }} ===Debut Year (2013)=== Faker originally started playing ''League of Legends'' under the name 고전파 (Which can be read as Go-Jeon-Pa or gojeonpa), and initially only played normal games. However, after stacking up on victories, his matchmaking rate ended up being so high that the queue times ended up taking too long, which made him switch to ranked play. Nearing the end of the second season of ranked play in 2012, Faker ended up being ranked second on the Korean ladder, and in the following season claimed the number one spot. {{cite web|url=https://www.invenglobal.com/articles/2117/rising-from-the-ashes-the-living-history-of-skt-t1-faker|title=Rising from the Ashes: The Living History of SKT T1 Faker|author=Kyeongbeom "Its" Kim, Sung Wook "Beckor" Baek, Woo "Ready" Hyun|publisher=Inven Global|date=2017-06-12}}{{cite web|url=https://www.invenglobal.com/articles/6756/skt-t1-faker-and-wolf-behind-the-scenes-faker-i-only-started-to-first-play-ranked-queue-because-i-couldnt-find-matches-in-normal-queue-anymore|title=SKT T1 Faker And Wolf Behind The Scenes. Faker: "I only started to first play ranked queue because I couldn't find matches in normal queue anymore."|author=James "Bick" Hong|publisher=Inven Global|date=2018-11-17}} At first Faker announced himself playing with an amateur team that consisted of himself, Bae "[[Bengi]]" Seong-woong, Kim "[[Ssumday]]" Chan-ho, and two other players. Later Faker was approached by coach Kim "[[kkOma]]" Jeong-gyun who was a coach for [[SK Telecom T1]], who offered him a position on a team. He was then officially announced as the first player for the sister team [[SK Telecom T1 2]] on February 6, 2013.{{cite web|url=https://m.inven.co.kr/webzine/wznews.php?idx=53363|title=SKT T1 '고전파' 이상혁 영입, 2팀 창단 초읽기|trans_title=SKT T1 recruits 'Gojeonpa' Lee Sang-hyeok, counting down to the creation of a second team|author=Jeon Ju-han|publisher=Inven|language={{Flag|kr}} Korean|date=2013-02-06}} With the signing, he also officially changed his gamertag to Faker from 고전파. The team was later fully revealed on February 28, officially named [[SK Telecom T1 K]], and saw the additions of Jeong "[[Impact]]" Eon-young, Bae "[[Bengi]]" Seong-woong, Chae "[[Piglet]]" Gwang-jin, and Lee "[[PoohManDu]]" Jeong-hyeon. {{cite web|url=https://www.inven.co.kr/webzine/news/?news=66258|title=SK텔레콤 T1 LOL팀, 팀명 변경. 1팀 2팀에서 'S'와 'K'로!|trans_title=SK Telecom T1 LOL Team, team name changed. From Team 1 and Team 2 to ‘S’ and ‘K’!|author=Seo Dong-yong|publisher=Inven|language={{Flag|kr}} Korean|date=2013-02-28}} The team debuted in [[Champions/2013/Spring|Champions Spring 2013]], and in the opening match against [[CJ Entus Blaze]] Faker would already break out in his first game. Facing off against Kang "[[Ambition]]" Chan-yong who at the time was seen as the country's premier mid laner. In that game Faker managed to secure a solo kill on Ambition to take First Blood, after which he also pushed the advantage by tower diving the bot lane, and killing their jungler after that, he secured four kills in under eight minutes, and led the team to a decisive series victory. {{cite web|url=https://www.inven.co.kr/webzine/news/?news=66258|title=The Makers of Faker Heroes of Heartbreak: Ambition’s Role in Forming Faker’s Reign|author=John Popko|publisher=Inven Global|language={{Flag|usuk}} English|date=2024-04-03}} {{Quote |quote = "The first time I went into the OngameNet booth? How was it... I was a little nervous. I didn't think I would be nervous, but I was nervous. It was amazing to go into a place I'd only seen on TV.

I solo-killed an Ambition player in that game, right? I think that’s how I started to become famous. It was the most memorable game, and it was the game I felt the happiest about after winning."|sign =Lee "Faker" Sang-hyeok |source ={{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111212941/https://sports.news.naver.com/news.nhn?oid=442&aid=0000006813|title=매거진S 페이커 "누구도 내 위에 있을 수 없다"|trans_title=Magazine S Faker: "No one can be above me"|publisher=Inven|language={{Flag|kr}} Korean|date=2014-10-17}}}} For the remainder of the tournament, Faker was the focal point of the team. He picked up over 36% of his team's kills and accrued a 133 kills in 20 games. In which he placed third overall in these statistics in the event. In addition, he also led the statistic of earned gold per minute and gold share. Even being the only player in the league to earn above 300 {{Abbr/GPM}}. Furthermore, he ranked second overall in creep score, Only [[Ambition]] finished further than him in CS per Minute, but he played games that were two and a half times longer than Faker's on average. {{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/-nq6ZUoXxqI|title=The Greatest Rookie Ever T1 Faker's Untold Story|publisher=Red Bull Gaming|language={{Flag|kr}} Korean|date=2022-08-10}} However despite his efforts the team eventually was defeated in the Semifinals, as they lost against the eventual champions, [[MVP Ozone]]. They were able to console themselves with a 3-0 victory against [[CJ Entus Frost]] to end the tournament in third overall. [[File:SKT Worlds 2013.jpg|thumb|right|460px|''Faker and SKT hoisting the [[World_Championship/2013|Season 3 World Championship trophy]]'']] Heading into [[Champions/2013/Summer|Champions 2013 Summer]] had continued to refine his efficiency. Leading the statistic of CS per minute with 9.4, alongside leading the game in earned gold per minute, again being the only player to hit above 300 while also maintaining a 12.6 kills and assists average per game. Powered by an unprecedentedly efficient approach to the game, [[SK Telecom T1 K|SKT]] went 6-0 in their group and only lost a single game on their way to the finals. At the finals, they had to face [[KT Rolster B|KT Rolster]] and initially found themselves behind 0-2 in the series. But in game three showed up with a great performance on [[Zed]], securing a 9/0/8 KDA, and bringing back the team in the series. With another victory in game four, the team had tied up the series. And now had to face off in a blind pick game five. This format led to the Zed mirror match-up against Yoo "[[Ryu]]" Sang-wook in the midlane. Although the game was already heavily in favour of SKT, it did birth one of ''League of Legends'' iconic moments as Faker outplayed Ryu. [https://youtu.be/-nq6ZUoXxqI As Faker was able to come back from a huge HP deficit by dodging Ryu's abilities in an intense display of mechanics and managed to kill Ryu]. Following the outplay, the series was closed out with SKT's victory, crowning themselves the champions of the tournament. Faker was also awarded the MVP award of the season. With their victory, they were seeded straight into the finals of the [[World_Championship/2013/Regional_Finals/South_Korea|Regional Finals]]. Here they'd again face off against [[KT Rolster B|KT Rolster]] who made their way through the bracket, and this time SKT won the series in a convincing 3-1 record, with KT even surrendering in the last game. With this victory, Faker was set to make his international debut at the [[World_Championship/2013|Season 3 World Championship]]. Heading into the tournament, Faker was already being seen as the world's best midlaner, if not the world's best player. Following an interview with [[Oh My God]]'s midlaner Yu "[[cool]]" Jiajun after OMG had won a game against SKT in the Group Stage, he stated how hard it was to kill Faker in the game, nicknaming him the ''Unkillable Demon King'', a nickname that would stick throughout time. Apart from their loss against OMG, SKT managed to beat all other teams in their group to secure a 7-1 record to secure their spot in the Quarterfinals where they had to face off against the [[Gamania Bears]] which they convincingly beat 2-0. It was only in the semifinals that SKT was tested as they faced off against fellow Korean team [[NaJin Black Sword]]. The series would be a back-and-forth going the distance, but ultimately SKT came out on top to qualify for the grand finals. Here they convincingly beat [[Royal Club]] in a 3-0 sweep, even closing out the third game in just over 20 minutes. With this victory, Faker had won his first Worlds title at just the age of 17. ===Sophomore Jinx (2014)=== After winning the [[World_Championship/2013|Season 3 World Championship]], Faker returned to the [[Champions/2013-2014/Winter|Champions Winter 2013-2014]], in which he dominated. Faker's domination continued until the beginning of [[Champions/2014/Spring|Champions Spring 2014]], recording 19 game win streak; a record that was not broken for the next 10 years.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/LCK/status/1813918619711254900|title=Congratulations on the incredible #LCK record, @GenG!|author=[[LCK]]|date=2024-07-18}} Despite the record, Faker ended [[Champions/2014/Spring|Champions Spring 2014]] in quarterfinals and ended the season as the {{Ordinal|3|sup=yes}} place in [[NLB/2014/Spring|NLB Spring 2014]]. Although Faker managed to win [[NLB/2014/Summer|NLB Summer 2014]] after ending [[Champions/2014/Summer|Champions Summer 2014]] at quarterfinals, qualifying for the [[Champions/2014/Regional_Finals|regional finals]], Faker failed to qualify for [[World Championship/2014|Worlds]]. ===SKT T1 Dynasty (2015-2016)=== At the end of 2014, the two sub-teams of [[SK Telecom T1|SKT T1]] were merged into one. With the merged team, Faker finished off the group stage of the [[LCK/2015/Spring|Spring]] season in the second place. After a reverse sweep of 3-2 against [[CJ Entus]] followed by a 3-0 sweep against [[GE Tigers]], Faker won his third LCK title, qualifying to the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2015|MSI]]. Despite ending the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2015|MSI]] as the runner-up, Faker's domination in the LCK continued in the [[LCK/2015/Summer|Summer]] season. Returning to [[World Championship/2015|Worlds]] two years after his first, Faker had become one of the first two players (the other being [[Bengi]]) to win two Worlds titles. Faker continued ruling the LCK, winning the [[LCK/2016/Spring|Spring]] season and then the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2016|MSI]], for which he was awarded the MVP. Despite having a slight pause in the domination in the [[LCK/2016/Summer|Summer]] season, ending it in the third place, Faker and [[SK Telecom T1|SKT T1]] qualified to [[World Championship/2016|Worlds]] as LCK's {{Ordinal|2|sup=yes}} seed. After a 3-2 in semifinals and another 3-2 in finals, Faker managed to defend his title, becoming the first two players (again, with [[Bengi]]) to win three Worlds titles. Faker was awarded the Finals MVP for Worlds, becoming the first player in LoL Esports history to win MVP in all international tournaments. {{Quote |quote=너무 많이 응원은 하지 마세요. 다음에 또 올 거니까.
[ Don't cheer too hard. We're going to come back anyway. ] |sign=[[Faker]] |source=Worlds 2016 Grand Final Post-match Interview{{cite web|url=https://www.gnewsbiz.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=5725|title=살아있는 전설 SKT! '2016 LoL 2016 월드 챔피언십'우승!|trans_title=Living Legend SKT! Wins 2016 LoL 2016 World Championship!|language={{FlagNoLink|kr}} Korean|author=이승수|publisher=경인경제|date=2016-11-03}}{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/o5dVuNVcWiY|title=The Words : Faker {{!}} Hall of Legends|author=|publisher=[[LCK|LCK Global]]|date=2024-05-24}} }} ===Fall of SKT T1 Dynasty (2017)=== Faker started the year strong by winning his sixth LCK title in [[LCK/2017/Spring|Spring 2017]], qualifying to the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2017|MSI]]. Faker and SKT T1 successfully defended the title, becoming the first team to win two consecutive [[MSI]]s. Despite having a bumpy ride in the [[LCK/2017/Summer|Summer]] season, Faker and SKT T1 managed to finish off the season as the runner-up, qualifying to [[World Championship/2017|Worlds]] as LCK's {{Ordinal|2|sup=yes}} seed. After finishing the group stage as group's first, Faker and SKT T1 returned to Finals after a 3-2 in quarterfinals against [[Misfits Gaming]] and another 3-2 in semifinals against [[Royal Never Give Up|RNG]]. In both matches, Faker stood as the last line of defense protecting the team. {{Quote |quote=You can beat [[SK Telecom T1|@sktelecom_t1]] but you can't beat Faker. |sign=[[Hans Sama]] |source={{cite web|url=https://x.com/Hanssama/status/921361203234033664|title=You can beat @sktelecom_t1 but you can't beat Faker.|author=[[Hans Sama]]|date=2017-10-20}} }} [[File:SKT T1 Faker Worlds 2017 Finals Post-match.jpg|thumb|right|460px|''Faker crying after [[World_Championship/2017|Worlds 2017]] Finals'']]In his {{Ordinal|4|sup=yes}} World Finals, Faker faced [[Samsung Galaxy]]. Despite his attempts to stand as the last line of defense, Faker had to allow a 0-3 sweep, failing to defend his title. Right after his loss, Faker collapsing and crying was caught on stream; something he had not shown publicly. {{Quote |quote=다 게임에만 몰빵한 친구들이거든요. 근데 그런 친구들이 눈물을 흘렸을 때는 정말 그만큼 절실하고 자기의 꿈이 있기 때문에, 그래서 눈물을 흘리는 거거든.
[ They're wholly committed to the game, these individuals. So when they cry it's because they're that invested and their dreams are that tangible; that's the source of their tears. ] |sign=[[starcraft:BoxeR|BoxeR]] |source={{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/MviIDKKvex0?t=5089|title=Retrospecto {{!}} T1 20th Anniversary Documentary|author=[[T1]]|date=2024-07-13}} }} ===Slumps and Struggles (2018-2021)=== ===First Season of ZOFGK Roster (2022)=== T1 started off the year with the [[Zeus]]-[[Oner]]-Faker-[[Gumayusi]]-[[Keria]] (ZOFGK) roster. Faker and T1 dominated the [[LCK/2022/Spring|Spring]] season, winning the season without a single match loss. During this season, Faker reached a total of 2500 kills in [[LCK]].{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/Caorro_Oahw/|title=THE LEGEND MAKES LEGEND|publisher=[[LCK]]|date=2022-03-03}} They finished the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2022|MSI]] as the runner-up, after a 2-3 loss against [[RNG]]. After finishing off the [[LCK/2022/Summer|Summer]] season as the runner-up, T1 qualified for [[World Championship/2022|Worlds]] as LCK's {{Ordinal|2|sup=yes}} seed. After finishing as the group's first place in the group stage, T1 advanced to the knockout stage. Although T1 managed to take a revenge against [[RNG]] in quarterfinals with a 3-0 sweep and proceed to finals after a 3-1 victory against [[JDG]] in the semifinals, T1's journey in Worlds ended with a 2-3 loss against [[DRX]] in finals. ===Return of the Emperor (2023)=== With the same ZOFGK roster as 2022, Faker and T1 started off the [[LCK/2023/Spring|Spring]] season with 17-1 in the group stage, but had to see [[Gen.G Esports|Gen.G]] lift up the trophy. One month after the beginning of the [[LCK/2023/Summer|Summer]] season, Faker had to take a break in July due to an injury in his right arm and hand.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/T1LoL/status/1676516269359603712|title=A Message from T1|publisher=[[T1|T1LoL]]|date=2023-07-05}} After taking a month's break, Faker returned in early August.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/T1LoL/status/1686625375575527425|title=A Message from 'Becker'|author=Jeong "Becker" Hoi-yoon|publisher=[[T1|T1LoL]]|date=2023-08-02}} Faker and T1 then were able to finish off the season as the runner-up, securing their spot in [[World Championship/2023|Worlds]] as LCK's {{Ordinal|2|sup=yes}} seed. [[File:T1 Faker Worlds 2023 Champion.jpg|thumb|right|460px|''Faker with the [[World_Championship/2023|2023 World Championship]] trophy'']]After winning the [[Asian Games/2022|Asian Games]] as the team captain, Faker made his eighth [[Worlds 2023|Worlds]] appearance with T1. Faker and T1 would make their way through the Swiss Stage by only dropping a game to [[Gen.G Esports]]. After sweeping [[BLG]] 2-0 in their last match of Swiss Stage, they first had to face off against [[LNG Esports]] from the [[LPL]]. As they entered the last quarterfinals match, after the fall of all other LCK teams in Worlds, T1 had become the "LCK's final hope"{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/RUWVgBceVdI|title=LNG vs T1 {{!}} SCOUT VS FAKER {{!}} Quarterfinals Day 4 Tease {{!}} Worlds 2023|author=|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2023-11-05}} by being the only team remaining in Worlds outside of the LPL. T1 was were able to sweep 3-0 against LNG. Their next opponent was [[JD Gaming]], a team that was looking to complete their "Golden Road" and were seen as the favourites to win the tournament. {{Quote |quote=[[Ruler]] 선수 잊지 말아야 할 겁니다. 모든 길은 결국 저를 통합니다.
[ [[Ruler]], you must not forget: All roads lead to me. ] |sign=[[Faker]] |source=Worlds 2023 Semifinals Day 2 Tease{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/mf72jNoMqL0?t=231|title=T1 vs JDG {{!}} LEGENDS NEVER DIE {{!}} Semifinals Day 2 Tease {{!}} Worlds 2023|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2023-11-12}} }} However, T1 was able to come out on top in the series with a 3-1 victory, putting a stop to [[JDG]]'s Golden Road. With their victory, Faker entered his sixth World Finals;{{cite web|url=https://x.com/lolesports/status/1723665978347905294|title=SIX. WORLD. FINALS. 🐐|author=LoL Esports|date=2023-11-12}} this time being faced with [[Weibo Gaming]]. {{Quote |quote=페이커! 7년 만에! 무려 7년 만에! 페이커가! 넥서스를 파괴하면서! 황제의 재림을 선언합니다!
[ Faker! After 7 years, after 7 long years! Faker! As he destroys the Nexus! Declares the return of the emperor! ] |sign=[[Caster Jun]] |source=Worlds 2023 Grand Final{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/dD3koK8zIhI?t=14973|title=WBG vs T1 {{!}} 결승전 {{!}} 2023 월드 챔피언십|trans_title=WBG vs T1 {{!}} Grand Final {{!}} 2023 World Championship|publisher=[[LCK]]|language={{FlagNoLink|kr}} Korean|date=2023-11-12}} }} T1 dominated the series and swept the final LPL team 3-0. With their victory, after 7 years since [[World Championship/2016|his last]], a decade since [[World Championship/2013|his first]], Faker had become the one and only 4-time World Champion. Later in the year, Faker was awarded the Mid of the Year and the Player of the Year in [[LCK/2023/Awards|LCK Awards 2023]]. ===Made Them Believe (2024)=== ===Earned His Legacy (2025)=== ==Gallery== SKT Faker Worlds 2013 .jpg|[[SK_Telecom_T1_K|SKT]] Faker at the [[World_Championship/2013|2013 World Championship]] SKT Faker MSI 2015.jpg|[[SK_Telecom_T1|SKT]] Faker at the [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2015|2015 Mid-Season Invitational]] Faker and Duke at the 2016 World Championship Semifinals.jpg|[[SK_Telecom_T1|SKT]] Faker and [[Duke]] at the [[World_Championship/2016|2016 World Championship]] Faker at MSI 2017 Finals.jpg|[[SK_Telecom_T1|SKT]] Faker at [[MSI 2017]] Finals SKT Faker 2018LCK.jpg|[[SK_Telecom_T1|SKT]] Faker at [[LCK/2018/Summer|LCK Summer 2018]] SKT Faker Worlds 2019.jpg|[[SK_Telecom_T1|SKT]] Faker at the [[World_Championship/2019|2019 World Championship]] T1 Faker at LCK 2020 Spring Finals.jpg|[[T1]] Faker at the [[LCK/2020/Spring|LCK 2020 Spring]] Finals T1 Faker Summer 2021.jpg|[[T1]] Faker at [[LCK/2021/Summer|LCK Summer 2021]] T1 Faker MSI 2022.jpg|[[T1]] Faker at [[MSI 2022]] T1 Faker at Worlds 2022.jpg|[[T1]] Faker at [[Worlds 2022]]'s Semifinal feature Faker Worlds 2022 Image 2.jpg|[[T1]] Faker at [[Worlds 2022]] T1 Faker MSI 2023.jpg|[[T1]] Faker at [[MSI 2023]] T1 Faker Worlds 2023.jpg|[[T1]] Faker at [[Worlds 2023]] T1 Faker MSI 2024.jpg|[[T1]] Faker at [[MSI 2024]] Faker HOL Media Day.jpg|[[Caster Jun]], Faker, and [[Youn Soo-bin]] at [[Hall of Legends]] Media Day. ==Media== {{Player Media}} ===Cheering Chant=== {{#ev:youtube|1PawA52_daA|600}} ==Trivia== * Faker attented the same high school (Mapo High School) as Kim "[[Deft]]" Hyuk-kyu.{{cite
